title: NimbleBay POC Weekly - prefetch & KV hit-rate review
topics: Next steps for pilot and benchmarks
summary: Weekly sync to review NimbleBay POC KV/prefix cache metrics, discuss prompt reuse strategy, and decide tuning steps for prefetch heuristics and eviction. Redwood SE presented new cache simulation results; customer flagged sporadic tail latency and mismatched tokenization leading to lower-than-expected hit rates. Agreed to run a larger synthetic replay and to try canonicalized prompt keys + relaxed eviction TTLs.
action_items: Matt Cho (Redwood) - run 100k-sample KV hit simulator with canonicalization on 2026-02-18
Liam O'Connor (NimbleBay) - provide 24h sample of production prompts (anonymized) by 2026-02-14
Nadia Chen (NimbleBay) - enable detailed tail-latency traces for next two days, share logs to shared drive by 2026-02-13
Sofia Martinez (Redwood AE) - send updated pricing estimate for dedicated pilot + burst capacity by 2026-02-16
next_steps: Run expanded KV-prefetch simulation with prefix canonicalization
Test relaxed eviction policy (TTL + LRU hybrid) in staging for 48h
Share security docs (SOC2 + network diagram) and pilot SOW
Schedule deep-dive on tokenization mismatch with tokenizer examples
transcript:
Header: 2026-02-11 15:00 UTC | Duration: 42m | Recording: yes
Attendees: Sofia, Matt, Daniel (Redwood); Priya, Liam, Nadia, Markus (NimbleBay)
Links shared: drive.google.com/drive/fake-nimblebay-poc-metrics, spreadsheet: nimblebay-poc-hitrate-2026-02-11.xlsx

[00:00] Sofia Martinez: alright everyone, thanks for joining, uh, quick roll call?
[00:06] Priya Desai: Priya here.
[00:08] Liam O'Connor: Liam, on the call.
[00:09] Nadia Chen: Nadia.
[00:11] Markus Berg: Markus.
[00:13] Matt Cho: Matt from Redwood.
[00:15] Daniel Ruiz: Daniel, CSM.
[00:17] Sofia Martinez: cool, thanks. Agenda — quick recap of last week's changes, matt will share updated hit-rate sim, then we go into prompt reuse heuristics and tail-latency items.

[02:02] Matt Cho: ok so I pushed the sim last night, it's in the sheet, key assumptions: 50k replayed requests, mixed user sessions, prefix lengths 16/32/64 tokens. We tried three canonicalization strategies: exact-string, whitespace-normalize, and tokenized-prefix (hashing token ids).
[02:30] Liam O'Connor: quick q — are you using our production tokenizer or the open-source one? we've seen subtle diffs.
[02:33] Matt Cho: good call — it's the open-source BPE variant, not your internal fast-tokenizer. that likely explains some mismatch, noted.
[03:10] Priya Desai: hit-rate numbers? we expected higher after last weeks prefetch bump.
[03:15] Matt Cho: baseline (no canonicalize) 35% kv hit overall. whitespace-normalize -> 42%. tokenized-prefix -> 57% in the sim. but caveat: when we mirror your actual tokenizer the tokenized-prefix drops to ~51%.
[04:02] Nadia Chen: so tokenization diffs cost ~6 percentage points, ok.
[04:10] Matt Cho: yeah, and TTL/eviction plays big role — with aggressive TTL 30s re-evict we lose another ~8 pts.
[04:22] Markus Berg: that matches what we saw — cold-starts on weekends spike eviction. our workload has 40% sessions that come back after 45s so 30s TTL is too aggressive.
[05:01] Sofia Martinez: hmm ok, so candidate action: longer TTL or LRU hybrid. matt?
[05:08] Matt Cho: we suggest LRU with soft-TTL 60s — eviction moves to least recently used but soft expiration tries to keep items for slightly longer if access pattern shows recurrence. In sims that recovered ~5-6%.
[05:40] Liam O'Connor: curious about prefix length — in our logs many queries are short, like 12-24 tokens, so longer prefix might be noise.
[05:50] Matt Cho: yeah, we show diminishing returns beyond 48 tokens for your dataset. tokenized-prefix with 32 token window was sweet spot in both hit-rate and latency.
[06:20] Priya Desai: tail-latency — we still get these 95-99 spikes that break our SLA. any correlation with cache misses?
[06:27] Daniel Ruiz: quick note: some of the 99 spikes were actually model fallback events when capacity was busy.
[06:35] Matt Cho: right, two sources: cache miss leads to full model run + KV warm-up, and routing/fallback to larger model variant when burst. Both multiply latency.
[07:01] Nadia Chen: we saw a recurring pattern at 03:xx UTC where a downstream cron kicks off and creates tails. i can share traces.
[07:09] Markus Berg: sometimes we're seeing small request bursts from background indexing — spikes are short but cause evictions and cascade.
[07:30] Sofia Martinez: ok, so mitigation: increase prefetch aggressiveness around known cron windows, and set route fallback thresholds. also consider isolated capacity for heavy background jobs.

[09:00] Matt Cho: back to sim details — we also tried prefix hashing into canonical keys to avoid whitespace/variant paraphrase. hashing reduced false negatives but increases false positives where different prompts map to same bucket; net +12% hit in sim but added ~1.3% wrong reuse (i.e., returned out-of-context cached completions).
[09:33] Priya Desai: wow wrong reuse is dangerous for us — can we detect staleness? or add a lightweight checksum?
[09:40] Matt Cho: yes, one approach is lightweight signature plus embeddings similarity check (cheap vector compare) prior to reuse. We can do a top-k lexical check then reuse if similarity > threshold. Adds a bit of compute but prevents obvious mis-reuse.
[10:12] Liam O'Connor: embeddings check cost? token cost vs model run?
[10:18] Matt Cho: for small signature vectors it's microseconds; in our infra it's a 0.5–1ms add on average, much cheaper than a full model run.
[10:35] Nadia Chen: would that change our billing model? we're on hosted trial now.
[10:40] Sofia Martinez: it's an infra/feature toggle; cost estimated in the updated pricing that i'll send. won't change token billing but may increase compute units slightly. we'll include it in the SOW options.

[12:25] Liam O'Connor: about canonicalization — can we just normalize case, strip punctuation and do unicode NFKC? that would handle a lot.
[12:33] Matt Cho: yes, we included NFKC+casefold+strip punctuation in whitespace-normalize variant. It got us from 35%->42%. The tokenized-prefix is better but heavier.
[13:05] Priya Desai: i still worry about user-specific slots, e.g., name placeholders. we need a step to anonymize or mask PII so cached keys are reusable across users.
[13:15] Sofia Martinez: agreed, Liam will deliver anonymized samples. we can run canonicalization + PII masking heuristics in sim.

[15:00] Matt Cho: quick demo — opening the spreadsheet, sheet "sim-results-Feb11"
[15:05] [screen share noise, garbled for a few seconds]
[15:20] Matt Cho: ok row 42 shows tokenized-prefix 32 window + soft TTL 60s => 54% overall kv hit, tail latency 99p reduced by ~18% compared to baseline.
[15:45] Priya Desai: that's promising. what's the false-reuse rate there?
[15:50] Matt Cho: ~1.1% in that config; with embeddings-check down to ~0.2% but hit-rate drops ~1 point. tradeoff.

[18:00] Markus Berg: curious about memory—if we increase TTL and keep more items, GPU memory or Redis size? what config are you simulating?
[18:08] Matt Cho: sim assumes a mid-sized Redis cluster, 128GB total for KV, eviction policy as described. With soft-TTL 60s, memory use went up ~22% in sim. we can push to dedicated Redis or use local in-GPU KV for hot prefixes to reduce network cost.
[18:35] Nadia Chen: local in-GPU KV sounds nice but ops complexity is higher; i'd prefer sticking to managed Redis for now.
[18:44] Matt Cho: totally reasonable. managed Redis + adjusted TTL is straightforward.

[20:10] Liam O'Connor: on the tokenizer mismatch — i'll run our fast-tokenizer on a 24h anonymized sample and send the token ids. will that help you re-run the sim?
[20:19] Matt Cho: perfect, that will make sim more realistic. if you can include session ids (hashed) we can measure inter-arrival and better simulate recency. please strip PII though.

[22:00] Priya Desai: another question: prompt engineering and canonicalization — we have a lot of micro-variants where users add adjectives, e.g., "cheap red shoes" vs "cheap & red shoes" — will canonicalization collapse useful signal?
[22:14] Matt Cho: risk exists; our tokenized-prefix keeps token-level detail but hashing risks collapse. That's why we like tokenized + embeddings-check: it gives high hit-rate while guarding against semantically different prompts. You can tune threshold for more conservative reuse.

[24:05] Nadia Chen: logs — i'll enable trace-level for two days and drop to the drive. which fields do you need? request id, timestamp, prompt raw, tokenized length, response latency.
[24:17] Matt Cho: that's perfect. also include model variant served, cache hit/miss flag, and whether prefetch fired.

[26:30] Sofia Martinez: pricing/ops — quick reminder, if you want dedicated capacity for the pilot we have a burst option to avoid fallback to larger models. sends costs.
[26:42] Priya Desai: what's the delta to avoid fallback? we can tolerate some higher cost if latency is stable.
[26:48] Sofia Martinez: order of magnitude: dedicated pilot with burst is roughly 20–30% uplift over hosted baseline for similar SLA — i'll send a one-pager, matt also add the compute delta for embeddings-check.

[29:10] Matt Cho: one more sim note — we tried mixing in background indexing load; prefetch with cron-aware schedule gained an extra 3-4% hit and reduced tails. So scheduling prefetch to run just after heavy jobs helps.
[29:35] Markus Berg: we can coordinate — i'll provide cron windows.

[31:00] Liam O'Connor: we should also consider a small A/B: canonicalization on 30% of traffic and measure UX regressions before full rollout.
[31:09] Matt Cho: yes, Redwood supports canary routing per prefix key or traffic percentage. we'll set up metrics to compare hit-rate and correctness.

[33:50] Priya Desai: on correctness: how do we capture false positives? can we log a sampling of reused responses and human-review?
[33:59] Daniel Ruiz: we can add a sampling hook to store pre/post reuse pairs in the review bucket, privacy controls applied.
[34:05] Nadia Chen: ok good. we'll assign a couple PMs to review.

[36:20] Markus Berg: minor item — SSO for the console, we need SAML config and audit logs forwarded to our SIEM. is that in the security pack?
[36:28] Sofia Martinez: yes — SOC2, SAML, and audit log forwarding included. i'll attach the security pack and the network diagram.

[38:05] Sofia Martinez: recap: 1) Liam provides anonymized 24h prompts + tokenizer output by 2026-02-14; 2) Matt runs 100k sim with tokenized-prefix + embeddings-check and soft-TTL 60s by 2026-02-18; 3) Nadia turns on tail traces and uploads logs by 2026-02-13; 4) Sofia sends pricing and security docs by 2026-02-16.
[38:30] Priya Desai: agreed.
[38:35] Liam O'Connor: i'll start on the data pull, should be able to get it to you Monday.
[38:40] Markus Berg: i'll share cron windows and ops notes.
[39:00] Matt Cho: quick note — we also put a short how-to deck in the drive about canonicalization options, link in the chat.
[39:12] Daniel Ruiz: i'll follow up with calendar invite for the tokenizer deep-dive next week, matt and liam to sync.
[40:00] Sofia Martinez: any other questions?
[40:03] Priya Desai: none from me. thanks.
[40:06] Nadia Chen: thanks all.
[40:10] Liam O'Connor: thanks.
[40:12] Matt Cho: thanks everyone.
[40:15] Sofia Martinez: bye.
